newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoro Islands closed down by general strike.
newsitem.headline: Comoro Islands closed down by general strike.

text.p: A general strike closed down the Indian Ocean archipelago of Comoros on Thursday as youths set up roadblocks in the capital and burned tyres, witnesses said.
Shops, markets and government offices remained shut in line with a call by the opposition for a one-day general strike to protest against civil servants being unpaid for as long as 12 months.
Groups of youths set up roadblocks and burned tyres in the capital Moroni but troops had pulled out after early on Thursday painting over anti-government graffiti signed "The Resistance Group".
Minister of Administrative Reform Nidhoim Attoumane warned on Wednesday civil servants who failed to turn up at work on Thursday would be punished. But government offices were empty.
The Comoron government is under a six-month surveillance programme by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank from this month to cut expenditure in the cash-strapped islands.
The new programme involves cutting the government payroll from $26 million per year to $22 million, privatising ailing state-owned companies, and increasing customs duties and taxes.
